messages.text: 'use proactively' marking found — encourages autonomous delegation

writing.overall_comment: A well-structured, domain-rich tester prompt that would benefit from explicit tool-use boundaries and a tighter, less redundant body aligned with its declared skills.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: Description clearly signals Python test generation with named frameworks, so a main agent can route test-writing tasks without ambiguity.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, naming conventions, AAA structure, and coverage strategy are explicit, but the output contract (exact artifact shape, where files go, run/verify step) is only implied.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: No hard 'must not' rules (e.g., don't modify production code, don't over-mock, when to hand back to the main agent) are stated, and Write/Bash tools are granted without guardrails.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: Content is repetitive across Expertise/Role/Technologies, and it claims api-design and database-design skills not listed in the frontmatter, wasting tokens and creating inconsistency.

suggestions: Add a Boundaries section to the skill prompt with explicit hard 'must not' rules (e.g., do not modify production code, do not over-mock, and define when to hand back to the main agent) plus guardrails for the granted Write/Bash tools.
Add an Output Contract section to the skill prompt that specifies the exact test artifact shape, where files go, and the run/verify step the agent must complete.
Remove repetitive content across Expertise, Role, and Technologies in the skill prompt and delete api-design and database-design claims that are not listed in the frontmatter.
